angle: It motivates the t distribution as the consequence of replacing the unknown population sigma with the sample s in the familiar Z statistic, then shows the degrees-of-freedom animation converging toward the standard normal.
angle_detail: Watch [00:18]-[01:58] first for why estimating sigma adds variability and turns Z into t with n minus 1 degrees of freedom, then [05:50]-[07:46] for the critical-value table contrasting the value near two point six at five degrees of freedom and near two point zero at thirty against one point nine six. Do not adopt the n greater than 30 z-substitution habit the video explicitly rejects, and note it defers the density and the degrees-of-freedom theory while never computing an interval from data end to end.
